title: Seasonal Rush Prep: A POS Supplies Checklist for Hospitality
description: Before the holiday or summer rush, run this POS supply checklist so registers, printers, and drawers don't fail at the worst moment.
body:
Every restaurant, café, and bar knows the seasonal rush is coming — the holidays, the summer tourist wave, the festival weekends. What they don't always plan for is the moment a receipt printer goes dark or a cash drawer jams in the middle of it. This checklist walks you through the POS supplies to audit before the crowds arrive, so your hardware keeps pace with the line instead of stopping it.

1. Receipt Paper: Count Every Printer, Not Just the Register

The fastest way to stall a rush is to run out of receipt paper at the busiest register. But the register isn't the only printer that matters. Walk the floor and write down every device that prints — the front register, the bar printer, the handheld or mobile terminal, and the card reader if it prints customer copies. Each one likely takes a different roll width.

  • Check the model number on every printer before you order.
  • Match each roll width (2¼", 3⅛", and mobile sizes) to its printer.
  • Keep at least one full backup box per printer, not per store.
  • Choose BPA-free rolls — your staff handles receipts all shift.

The rule of thumb: if you're about to hit your busy season, order enough to cover the entire rush, not just a week of it. Reordering mid-season means paying for rush shipping or, worse, watching a printer sit idle.

2. Kitchen Printer Paper and Ribbons: The Forgotten Consumable

Kitchen printers work in the harshest conditions in the building — heat, grease, steam, and a nonstop stream of tickets. If you run an impact printer, it needs two consumables, not one: the paper and the ribbon. Owners remember the paper and forget the ribbon until tickets start printing light and unreadable, which is the last thing a line cook wants to squint at during a dinner rush.

  • Order ribbons in the same cycle as paper so both run out together.
  • Set a weekly reminder to check kitchen printer output for fading.
  • If you run thermal kitchen printers, confirm you have enough thermal stock for back-of-house.

An unreadable kitchen ticket doesn't just slow one order — it backs up the entire line. During a rush, that's revenue walking out the door.

3. Cash Drawers, Tills, and Small Change

Cash still moves in plenty of hospitality businesses, and a cash drawer is only as useful as what's inside it. Before a busy stretch, make sure your drawer is stocked and your change float is healthy. Running out of quarters or hand-writing coin totals mid-shift slows every cash transaction.

  • Replenish the float of small bills and coins daily during peak season.
  • Order coin wrappers and bank straps in bulk — they don't go bad.
  • Check that the drawer itself opens smoothly and the latch isn't sticking.
  • Consider a backup till so opening and closing counts never overlap.

A drawer that sticks or a float that's short is the kind of small failure that compounds across a hundred cash transactions in a single day.

4. Printer Maintenance: Cleaning Cards and Cables

Thermal printers don't need ink, but their print heads and rollers still collect dust, lint, and paper residue. During a high-volume season, that buildup causes faded receipts, paper jams, and misaligned printing — all at the worst possible moment. A pack of cleaning cards, run through the printer the same way you'd run a receipt, clears residue in seconds.

  • Run a cleaning card through every thermal printer before the rush begins.
  • Check cables and connections — a loose power or data cable is a common mid-shift failure.
  • Keep a spare power supply or cable on hand for your most critical printers.

Maintenance is the cheapest insurance on this list. Five minutes of cleaning now prevents a printer swap during your busiest hour.

5. The Walk-the-Floor Audit

The real work of rush prep isn't buying — it's the audit. Spend one walk of the floor writing down every printer's make, model, and roll size, plus the condition of each cash drawer and terminal. That single list becomes your ordering guide and your emergency reference when something inevitably needs a quick fix.

  • Note the model number and roll width for every printer.
  • Count current stock of paper, ribbons, and cleaning cards against your busy-season needs.
  • Flag anything worn — cables, drawer latches, faded print heads.
  • Set a reorder reminder so you're never caught short mid-season.

The pattern across every item is the same: the supply you don't think about is the one that stops your line. A seasonal rush magnifies small gaps into big problems.

Get Ahead of the Rush

The busiest weeks of the year are no time to discover your receipt paper doesn't match your printer or your kitchen ribbon ran out. Walk the floor, write down every device, and stock the backups to match — before the crowds arrive. The goal isn't more stuff in the back room; it's a register, kitchen, and drawer that never miss a beat when it matters most.
